title: Kranjska Gora, Vogel & Krvavec: A Julian Alps Ski Week
subRegion: Julian Alps & Gorenjska, Kranjska Gora, Planica, Bohinj and the Kamnik-Savinja fringe

bestPeriod.window: Mid-January-early March, with February the only month all four ski areas reliably run their full lift fleets
bestPeriod.avoid: 26 December-2 January, when Kranjska Gora fills with Italian and Croatian traffic; and the second week of March, when the Vitranc Cup and Planica ski-flying finals take over the valley
bestPeriod.raw: Mid-January-early March, with February the only month all four ski areas reliably run their full lift fleets

accommodation.note: Kranjska Gora 3-4 B&B €70, €120 pppn; Bohinjska Bistrica 20-30% less

food.note: Mountain restaurant mains €12, €20; valley dnevno kosilo €10, €15; Slovenian wine by the glass €3, €5

transport.note: Hire car €35, €55/day, e-vinjeta 7-day ≈ €16, fuel; airport transfer €60, €90 if not driving

activities.note: Kranjska Gora multi-day pass, Vogel and Krvavec day tickets, Planica, Pokljuka, one spa entry

profile.difficultyNote: 3/5, five lift-served days on modest vertical, one long snowshoe or cross-country day on the Pokljuka plateau, and a lot of driving between areas

gatewayAirport: LJU Ljubljana Jože Pučnik, 60 km / 50 min to Kranjska Gora, 8 km to the Krvavec cable car, 65 km / 1 h to Bohinj; VCE Venice Marco Polo 3 h and KLU Klagenfurt 1 h 30 as alternates
summary: Slovenia's ski week is not about one big mountain, there isn't one, but about four genuinely different ones inside an hour of each other, tied together by a hire car and a €16 vignette. **Kranjska Gora** is the World Cup village, low and tree-lined under the Vitranc ridge, with the **Podkoren** slalom and giant slalom courses on its doorstep and the **Planica** ski-flying hill five minutes up the valley. **Vogel**, reached by cable car from the shore of **Lake Bohinj**, is the opposite: a high shelf above a lake, with the best views and the most serious off-piste in the country. **Krvavec** sits eight kilometres from Ljubljana airport and delivers the highest, most reliable snow of the four. **Cerkno**, over the ridge in the Idrija hills, is the local's alternative when the Julian Alps are in cloud. The arc of the week runs Kranjska Gora first for the racing history and the easy legs, Vogel in the middle for the drama, Krvavec for altitude, and a full day on the **Pokljuka** biathlon plateau on snowshoes or skinny skis when the alpine legs need a break. It suits intermediates who would rather see four mountains than lap one, and anyone who values a €14 dinner and a thermal pool at the end of the day over lift-served vertical.

itinerary.title: Ljubljana, the e-vinjeta, and up to Kranjska Gora
itinerary.morning: Land at **LJU**, collect the hire car, and, before you touch the motorway, buy the **e-vinjeta** online or at a petrol station. It is electronic and registration-plate-linked; a 7-day car vignette is around €16 and driving the A2 without it is an expensive fine.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive the A2 north through the Karavanke foothills, turn off at Jesenice and run up the valley to **Kranjska Gora**, roughly 60 km and 50 minutes. Collect hire gear at **Intersport Bernik**, then walk out to the frozen **Jasna** lake at the foot of the Vršič road for the first view of the Julian Alps.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Gostilna Pri Martinu** in the village, a proper Slovenian *gostilna* doing *ričet*, sausage and buckwheat *žganci* at prices that will surprise anyone arriving from Austria.
itinerary.dayStats: LJU-Kranjska Gora 60 km / 50 min / e-vinjeta 7-day ≈ €16 / village 800 m / hire gear €95, €150 for six days

itinerary.title: Vitranc, Podkoren and the World Cup slope
itinerary.morning: Buy a Kranjska Gora day or multi-day ticket (**€49 adult, €30 child**) and ride up **Vitranc**. The village side is gentle and tree-lined; use it to warm up, then traverse west along the treeline toward **Podkoren**.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski the **Podkoren** sector, where the **Vitranc Cup** slalom and giant slalom are run each March. Outside race preparation the public gets the course, and it is a genuinely steep, icy, technical pitch that will tell you the truth about your edges.
itinerary.evening: Drive five minutes up the valley to **Planica** for the floodlit view of the **Letalnica bratov Gorišek**, then eat back in the village at **Kotnik Bistro & Pizzeria**, or upgrade to **Restavracija Milka** by Lake Jasna for the valley's fine-dining option.
itinerary.dayStats: Kranjska Gora 800-1,295 m, ≈ 20 km over 18 runs / day pass €49 adult / lifts to 16:00 / night skiing €36 if you have anything left

itinerary.title: Vogel: the cable car, Šija and Žagarjev graben
itinerary.morning: Drive 55 km round to **Ukanc** at the western end of **Lake Bohinj**, about an hour, and take the **Vogel cable car**, which lifts you from roughly 569 m at the lakeshore to 1,535 m in a single, slightly alarming span. Buy the day ticket at **€45 adult / €23 child**.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski the **Orlove glave** and **Šija** sectors, working up toward 1,800 m; the views back down over the lake and out to Triglav are the best in the country. If conditions and the ARSO bulletin allow, look at **Žagarjev graben**, Slovenia's best-known lift-accessed steep descent, and not a place to go on a whim.
itinerary.evening: Eat at **Gostilna Rupa** in Srednja vas, ten minutes from the lake, for game, *štruklji* and mountain cheese; or **Restavracija Foksner** in Bohinjska Bistrica for something more modern.
itinerary.dayStats: Vogel cable car 569 m → 1,535 m, ski area to ≈ 1,800 m / ≈ 22 km of piste / day pass €45 / **the cable car is the only way down, check the last descent time**

itinerary.title: Krvavec: the high mountain and the airport hill
itinerary.morning: Drive southeast to **Cerklje na Gorenjskem**, about 70 km, and ride the gondola from **Base 1450**. Krvavec is the highest and most reliable of the four, **1,450 to 1,971 m on Zvoh**, and it is eight kilometres from Ljubljana airport, which makes it the classic first-and-last-day option too.
itinerary.afternoon: Lap the reds off Zvoh and work the broader intermediate terrain; Krvavec has roughly 30 km, the most of any single area on this trip, and its snow holds when Kranjska Gora is struggling. Day ticket **€45 adult / €28 child**.
itinerary.evening: Drive back to Kranjska Gora, about 1 h 15, or detour to **Bled** and eat at a lakeside *gostilna* before the last leg. If it is Friday or Saturday, note that the Krvavec cable car runs late (to 20:00 Friday, 21:00 Saturday) for night events.
itinerary.dayStats: Krvavec 1,450-1,971 m, ≈ 30 km / day pass €45 / 6-day €198 adult, €112 child / drive from Kranjska Gora ≈ 70 km, 1 h 10-1 h 20

itinerary.title: Weather-contingency and rest day: Pokljuka, Planica and thermal water
itinerary.morning: This is the designed flex day, take it early if a föhn has stripped the low pistes or the Julian Alps are socked in, otherwise take it here. Drive up to **Rudno polje on the Pokljuka plateau, about 1,345 m**, Slovenia's biathlon World Cup venue, and either hire cross-country skis on the 35-40 km trail network or take the marked **snowshoe routes** through the spruce.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop back down and do **Planica** properly: the **Nordic Centre**, the base of the **Letalnica**, and, if it is running, the zipline down the ski-flying hill's landing slope, which is the fastest legal way to understand what those athletes are doing.
itinerary.evening: Thermal water. **Vodni park Bohinj** at the Bohinj ECO Hotel in Bohinjska Bistrica is the closest and the cheapest; **Wellness Živa** at Bled is the more comfortable. Dinner afterwards at **Gostilna Danica**.
itinerary.dayStats: Pokljuka plateau ≈ 1,345 m, 35-40 km of groomed trails / snowshoe circuits 2-4 h / zero alpine vertical / spa entry €15, €30 / Kranjska Gora-Pokljuka ≈ 50 km

itinerary.title: Second Vogel day, or Cerkno if the Julians are shut
itinerary.morning: Decide on the ARSO forecast. If the Julian Alps are clear, go back to **Vogel**, one day is never enough there, and the second visit is when you actually ski **Šija** and the upper bowls properly rather than gawping at the lake. If the Julians are in cloud and the Kranjska Gora pistes are thin, drive over to **Cerkno** in the Idrija hills instead, which sits in a different weather shadow and has roughly 18 km of well-made snow.
itinerary.afternoon: Whichever you chose, finish by 15:00 and drive round to **Lake Bohinj** for the walk along the northern shore to the **Church of St John the Baptist** at Ribčev Laz, fourteenth-century frescoes, no crowds in February.
itinerary.evening: Last dinner at **Štrud'l** in Srednja vas, or back in Kranjska Gora at **Gostilna Pri Martinu** for a repeat of the thing you liked on day one.
itinerary.dayStats: Vogel 1,535-1,800 m or Cerkno to ≈ 1,300 m, ≈ 18 km / drive Kranjska Gora-Cerkno ≈ 90 km, 1 h 30 / Bohinj lake circuit walk 4.5 km one way

itinerary.title: Krvavec morning, then the airport
itinerary.morning: The best last day in Slovenia: **Krvavec is eight kilometres from Ljubljana airport**. Check out, drive to Base 1450, ski until noon on a half-day or hourly ticket, and hand the skis back at the base.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop down to **LJU** in fifteen minutes. If you have longer, spend the spare hours in **Ljubljana** itself, the old town, the market colonnade and the castle funicular are a good decompression, and return the car at the airport rather than in the city.
itinerary.evening: Fly out. If the flight is early the next morning, sleep in Kranj or at an airport hotel rather than driving down from the mountains at dawn.
itinerary.dayStats: Krvavec base to LJU 8 km / 15 min / half-day or 2-5 hour tickets available / chip card deposit refunded on return / allow 2 h at LJU

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Kotnik
accommodationStrategy.description: A yellow-fronted family hotel in the middle of the village, a five-minute walk from the Vitranc lifts, with its own bistro and pizzeria downstairs and secure ski storage. It is the right base for a car-based week: central for the Planica and Podkoren end of the valley, cheap enough to leave budget for four separate lift tickets, and small enough that breakfast happens when you need it. Roughly €80, €130 per room.

accommodationStrategy.name: Bohinj ECO Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: The alternative axis: sleep near **Lake Bohinj** rather than Kranjska Gora, put **Vogel** twenty minutes away instead of an hour, and get **Vodni park Bohinj** attached to the building for the rest day. Pokljuka is also closer from here. The trade is a longer daily drive to Kranjska Gora and Krvavec. Roughly €90, €150 per room.

accommodationStrategy.name: Ramada Resort Kranjska Gora
accommodationStrategy.description: The family option, at the foot of the Kranjska Gora slopes with pool, ski room and enough rooms to absorb a group. Choose it for ski-in convenience and for the pool on a bad-weather afternoon rather than for character. Roughly €120, €200 per room.

logistics.connectivity: Coverage is good across all four resorts and in the valleys. Slovenia is **inside EU roaming**, so EU and (under most tariffs) UK bundles work at home rates, this is the one country on the Balkan ski circuit where you do not need to think about it. Download offline maps for the Pokljuka plateau, where forest cover degrades GPS.
logistics.emergency: **112** for everything; mountain rescue is the **Gorska reševalna zveza Slovenije (GRZS)**, which is professional, well-equipped and helicopter-capable. Slovenia is **in the EU and in Schengen**, so **EHIC/GHIC applies** for state healthcare, but it does not cover mountain rescue costs or repatriation, so carry winter-sports insurance regardless.
logistics.weather: Two phenomena matter. The **föhn** descending off the Karavanke can lift the freezing level a thousand metres in a few hours and ruin Kranjska Gora's low pistes overnight. And the **Adriatic low**, which drives moist air up against the Julian Alps, produces very heavy snowfall at Bohinj and Vogel, this is one of the wettest corners of the Alps, with wet-snow avalanche cycles to match. Fog fills the Ljubljana basin for days at a time in winter while the mountains sit in sun.
logistics.bookingWindows: Season passes are cheapest in the autumn presale. Beds in Kranjska Gora for the **Vitranc Cup and the Planica ski-flying finals in March** are effectively unobtainable inside two months, check the FIS calendar before you fix dates. Vogel and Krvavec day tickets need no advance purchase. Guided touring days should be booked at least a week out.
logistics.money: The **euro**. Cards are accepted essentially everywhere including mountain huts; carry €20, €30 in coins for parking and lockers. Tipping is rounding up, 5-10% in a restaurant.
logistics.transportRules: The **e-vinjeta** is mandatory on Slovenian motorways and expressways, it is electronic and linked to your registration plate, bought online at evinjeta.dars.si or at petrol stations and border kiosks. A **7-day car vignette is around €16, a month around €32, a year around €117.50**; hire cars usually come with an annual one, but verify. **Winter equipment is legally required from 15 November to 15 March** (and in winter conditions at any time): winter tyres, or summer tyres with chains carried and at least 3 mm tread. The **Vršič pass is closed** above the hairpins in winter. Lift access is by RFID chip card with a small refundable deposit.
logistics.permits: **Triglav National Park** covers Bohinj, Vogel's upper reaches and Pokljuka, camping, fires and off-trail driving are prohibited and drone use requires permission. Parking at Ukanc, Rudno polje and the Krvavec base is charged. Ski patrol closures are enforced.
logistics.health: Tap water is excellent everywhere and Slovenians drink it by default. The **ARSO avalanche bulletin at meteo.arso.gov.si** is issued daily through the winter on the EAWS 1-5 scale and is the source to read before any off-piste or touring, it is properly resourced, unlike most of the region. Altitude is a non-issue below 2,000 m.

proTips: If you will ski more than about twelve days a season in Slovenia, the **Vogel season pass at €584 is the smart buy**, it is valid at Kranjska Gora too, which no single-resort ticket elsewhere in the country matches.

Buy the **e-vinjeta before you leave the airport car park**, not at the first motorway sign. It is registration-linked and takes two minutes online; the fine for driving without one starts at several hundred euros.

**Ski Krvavec on your arrival or departure day.** It is eight kilometres from the terminal, which turns two travel days into two half-ski days and is the single best piece of scheduling available in this country.

Ask at the Kranjska Gora lift office whether **Podkoren 3** is open to the public. Outside race preparation weeks it usually is, and skiing a live World Cup slalom course is not something most resorts allow.
Check the **last cable car down from Vogel** on the morning you go, and write it on your hand. When the lower mountain is bare there is no ski-home and no road, the cable car is the only exit.
Go to **Pokljuka on a bluebird day, not a bad one**. The plateau at 1,345 m under a hard blue sky with the Triglav massif behind it is the best half-day of the week, and it is wasted in flat light.
Eat lunch in the valley, not on the mountain. A *dnevno kosilo* (daily set lunch) in Bohinjska Bistrica or Kranjska Gora runs €10, €15 for three courses; the same money on the hill buys a sandwich.

Read the **ARSO bulletin yourself** before touching Žagarjev graben or the Šija bowls. Slovenia publishes a real EAWS bulletin, a rarity in this part of Europe, and it is far better than any hotel's verbal summary.
If March dates are unavoidable, either commit to the **Vitranc Cup and Planica** and book beds four months out, or base yourself at Bohinj and let Kranjska Gora have its circus without you.

raw.Pass tiers by name: Slovenia has no single Alpine-style area ticket; you buy **resort passes** and, if you are staying put, a **season pass with cross-resort validity**. **Kranjska Gora (RTC Žičnice Kranjska Gora)**: **day adult €49, child €30, youth €33, senior €44**; **season pass €550 adult / €440 youth / €330 child**; **night skiing €36**; a **2 adults + 2 children family day at €135**; consecutive multi-day tickets run from **€90 for a 2-day adult to €364 for a 10-day adult (child 10-day €198)**, with **hourly 2-5 hour tickets** for short days. **Vogel**: **day adult €45, child (6-14.99) €23, youth/senior €39**; **2-day €82 / €42 / €71**; **6-day €213 / €111 / €185**; **season €584 / €346 / €478**, and critically **the Vogel season pass is also valid at Kranjska Gora**, which is the closest thing Slovenia has to a regional super-pass. **Krvavec (RTC Krvavec)**: **day adult €45, child €28, youth/senior €41**; **6-day €198 / €112 / €178**; **season €649 / €439 / €599**, with a **Monday-Friday season pass at €529** that becomes all-day from 15 March. Cable-car-only tickets exist for non-skiers: **Vogel return €22 adult / €11 child**, **Krvavec return €18 / €13**. **Chip card deposit is €3 at Vogel** and comparable elsewhere, refunded on return. Buy online through each resort's site for the autumn presale discount on season passes; day and multi-day tickets are fixed-price and not dynamic.
raw.Lift network and interconnects: These are four separate lift systems with **no ski link between any of them**, the connection is the road. **Kranjska Gora** runs from about **800 m in the village to 1,295 m on Vitranc**, with a chain of chairs and drags spreading west along the treeline to the **Podkoren** sector, home of the **Vitranc Cup** World Cup slalom and giant slalom. From Podkoren it is a five-minute drive to **Planica**, where the **Letalnica bratov Gorišek** ski-flying hill and the **Planica Nordic Centre** cross-country loops sit at the head of the valley. **Vogel** is reached by the **Ukanc cable car**, which lifts from about **569 m at Lake Bohinj to 1,535 m** in one span, the ski area then climbs to roughly **1,800 m** across the sectors **Orlove glave**, **Šija**, **Rjava skala** and **Zadnji Vogel**, with the **Žagarjev graben** dropping steeply off the northern side. **Krvavec** starts with the gondola from **Base 1450** at Cerklje and tops out on **Zvoh at 1,971 m**. **Cerkno** runs to about 1,300 m on Črni Vrh. **Last lifts are 16:00 across the board**, and the operational trap is Vogel: **the cable car is the only way down when the lower slopes are bare, and its last descent is the hard stop of your day**, miss it and there is no road. The Bohinj and Gorenjska ski-bus services patch the valley in season, but a hire car is what actually makes this week work.
raw.Snow reliability: **Krvavec 1,450-1,971 m** is the most reliable, high base, north-facing, and it typically opens first and closes last. **Vogel 1,535-1,800 m** has a high base but a small vertical band and sits close enough to the Adriatic to catch warm, wet fronts. **Kranjska Gora 800-1,295 m is the weak link**: low, sheltered and almost wholly dependent on snowmaking, which the resort runs hard and well on the Vitranc and Podkoren pistes. **Cerkno**, at up to 1,300 m, is similarly snowmaking-led. Published seasons run roughly **1 December to early May at Krvavec (to 5 May) and Vogel (season pass valid to 9 May)**, with the honest window mid-December to late March. **None of the four publishes snowmaking coverage as a percentage of pisted kilometres**, treat any figure quoted to you as marketing. In a bad snow year the pattern is predictable: Kranjska Gora runs a snowmade ribbon on Vitranc and Podkoren and nothing else, Vogel keeps its upper bowl and closes the ski-home, and everyone drives to Krvavec.
raw.Off-piste and touring: The real terrain is at **Vogel**: **Žagarjev graben**, the steep gully off the north side, is the country's best-known lift-accessed descent and is serious in the wrong conditions; the bowls under **Šija** at around 1,800 m give the widest open off-piste in Slovenia; and from the top of the area you can tour toward **Rodica** and the **Črna prst** ridge. Kranjska Gora's off-piste is limited tree skiing; Krvavec has good short lines off **Zvoh**. Ski touring proper happens on the **Pokljuka plateau**, on the **Vršič** road approaches (the pass itself is closed above the hairpins in winter), and in the Kamnik-Savinja Alps. **Slovenia does publish a proper daily EAWS avalanche bulletin**, from **ARSO, the Slovenian Environment Agency (meteo.arso.gov.si)**, on the standard 1-5 European scale, and it is good. There is no legal guide requirement, but the Julian Alps produce a persistent-weak-layer snowpack and the terrain above Bohinj is unforgiving; hire through the **Združenje gorskih vodnikov Slovenije** (Slovenian Mountain Guides Association) or a Bled-based operator such as **3glav Adventures**. Expect €250, €400 per day for a guided group.
raw.Piste breakdown: **Kranjska Gora: roughly 20 km over 18 runs, heavily blue and red, with the Podkoren FIS courses as the only genuine steeps. Vogel: roughly 22 km, mostly red, with Žagarjev graben as the black. Krvavec: roughly 30 km, the broadest spread of the four and the best intermediate mileage. Cerkno: roughly 18 km.** That is around **90 km across the week**, which is a single Alpine sector, the point here is variety, not volume. **Beginners** belong on Kranjska Gora's village nursery slopes and the wide lower Krvavec pistes. **Intermediates** should spend their money at **Krvavec**, which has the most red kilometres and the most consistent snow. **Experts** get exactly three things worth travelling for: the **Podkoren 3 World Cup course** when it is open to the public outside race week, **Žagarjev graben** at Vogel, and the touring above Bohinj.
raw.Non-ski days: **Planica** is the standout: the **Letalnica bratov Gorišek**, the ski-flying hill where the world distance record has repeatedly been set, plus the **Planica Nordic Centre** with its cross-country trails, wind tunnel and zipline down the hill's landing slope. The **Pokljuka plateau at Rudno polje (about 1,345 m)** is Slovenia's biathlon World Cup venue and gives 35-40 km of groomed cross-country trails and superb marked snowshoe routes through spruce forest. For warm water: **Vodni park Bohinj** at the Bohinj ECO Hotel in Bohinjska Bistrica, **Wellness Živa** at Bled, and **Terme Snovik** about an hour east, Slovenia's thermal culture is genuinely good and cheap. Add **Lake Bled** and its island, the **Zelenci** springs above Kranjska Gora, and the frozen **Jasna** lake.
raw.Hire, lockers and schools: **Intersport Bernik** in Kranjska Gora is the long-established rental and service shop in the valley; each resort also runs its own rental at the base or top station, Vogel's being at the cable car's upper terminal. Expect **€20, €30/day** for a standard package, **€95, €150 for six days**; performance skis add 40-50%. Lockers €4, €8/day. Instruction runs through the **Smučarska šola Kranjska Gora (ASK Kranjska Gora)**, the **Vogel** and **RTC Krvavec** ski schools: roughly **€45, €65 an hour for a private lesson** and **€160, €240 for a five-morning group course**. English is universally available and the standard of teaching is high, Slovenia is a serious racing nation with instructors to match.
